context: Options to weigh rather than a fixed design: (a) have fast_lane_ratchet_check.py report consumption against the most recent entry stated purpose so erosion is visible before it forces a bump; (b) record a per-program reserved allotment in the policy JSON that the PR-lane delta guard reads; (c) accept erosion and bump on a schedule, treating the log entry rationale as narrative only. Prior art: _project/config/fast_lane_ceiling_log.md convention header, docs/operations/fast-lane-budget.md, scripts/fast_lane_ratchet_check.py.
description: The quantum convention (+500, headroom floor 250) assumes a bump buys runway for the work that motivated it, but nothing binds the reservation to that work. The 2026-08-04 entry bumped 27050->27550 and stated its purpose explicitly: the one-engine program had eight items still to land, three of which add parity and characterization suites. Between #1567 and #1600 roughly 30 unrelated PRs (results-privacy identifier drops, submit terminal-state classification, CI plumbing, tracker tooling, quality guards) took the lane from 26834 to 27278 -- consuming 444 of the 716 reserved -- while zero one-engine items landed, forcing a fifth standalone ceiling PR (#1611) one day later. This is now a repeating shape: five quantum-convention bumps, three of them carrying no test-count change of their own, and the 2026-08-03 entry documents a crossing that produced two misattributed auto-revert PRs (#1491, #1492). The convention successfully ended minimal-headroom bumps but does not make a reservation legible to the next PR author, so headroom is consumed first-come rather than as budgeted.

preserves.behavior: The +500 quantum and the 250 headroom floor stay in force; this adds visibility, it does not relax the ceiling.
The ceiling remains the enforced backstop in --strict, make ci-lint, and develop-post-merge.yml.
